body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{lb}}\le C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{ub}}<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\), such that \(c_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{lb}}\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\le\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le C_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{ub}}\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\). The infimum defining \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\) ranges over all schedule-independent Markov kernels from the observed assignment--outcome record to closed intervals, including auxiliary-randomized and variable-length procedures, and both coverage and expected length use the same extended design law.
body.justification: The sandwich gives operational meaning to the average-design optimized radius as the information frontier for honest NCC inference.
body.gap: LeeWason2020 and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift evaluate parametric or model-based time adjustments for platform controls, while ChenLiZhangYe2025 Theorem 4 gives a Gaussian bounded-confounding confidence-interval-length rate and attaining upper construction, ChenLiZhangYe2025 Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility, and the Gaussian convex-class results of CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 establish minimax expected-length conclusions for Gaussian observation experiments. No published result gives an all-kernel expected-length lower bound for availability-constrained adaptive randomization over fixed schedules with TV-bounded control drift.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a certificate that a chosen drift budget buys nearly the shortest possible uniformly honest observed-data interval.
body.proof_tex:
The upper bound is immediate from Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm:honest\text{-}upper\text{-}frontier}\).  That theorem constructs a single schedule-independent kernel \(K^\star\in\mathcal C_\alpha\) and proves
\[
\sup_{Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,\Gamma}}
\mathbb E^{K^\star}_{\mathcal D,Y}[\operatorname{len}(I^\star)]
\le 2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(K\in\mathcal C_\alpha\), as required by Definition~\(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}minimax\text{-}length}\), gives
\[
\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\le2\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star.
\]
For the other unconditional inequality, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem:mixture\text{-}modulus\text{-}length\text{-}lower\text{-}bound}\), applied at \(\eta_\alpha=(1-2\alpha)/2\), gives directly
\[
\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star
\ge \eta_\alpha\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta_\alpha).
\]
Both bounds therefore hold for every experiment covered by the frozen assumptions.

It remains to show that the proposed lower comparison with \(\mathfrak R_\alpha^\star\) is false, rather than merely unavailable from the current proof.  Fix the declared \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) and \(M>0\), and put
\[
\varepsilon=\frac\alpha2,
\qquad
\delta_n=\frac{\varepsilon}{n}.
\]
For every sufficiently large integer \(n\), construct the following admissible experiment.  Take \(B=3\), \(W=\{2\}\), \(q_2=1\), and block sizes \((n_1,n_2,n_3)=(1,n,1)\).  Add one arm label \(a\notin\{z_0,z_1\}\), and set
\[
A_1=\{z_0,a\},
\qquad
A_2=\{z_0,z_1\},
\qquad
A_3=\{z_0\}.
\]
At the sole position in block \(1\), assign \(a\) with probability \(\varepsilon\) and \(z_0\) with probability \(1-\varepsilon\).  Define the predictable event
\[
E=\{Z_{11}=a\}.
\]
It is known before block \(2\) and has probability \(\varepsilon\) under every fixed schedule.  At every position in block \(2\), for every compatible history, set
\[
p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})=
\begin{cases}
\delta_n,&E,\\
1/2,&E^c,
\end{cases}
\qquad
p_{2i}(z_0\mid H_{2i})=1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i}).
\]
At block \(3\), assign \(z_0\) with probability one.  These conditional probabilities define the assignment law and hence satisfy sequential randomization.  They are measurable with respect to the pre-assignment histories, their support is exactly the displayed availability set, and, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every available-arm probability is at least
\[
p_{\min,n}=\delta_n>0.
\]
Thus the sequential-randomization, availability-window, availability-support, and propensity-floor assumptions all hold.  Take \(\Gamma=0\); the schedule class remains the set of all bounded fixed potential outcomes whose three control block means are equal, so the bounded-outcome and control-total-variation assumptions also hold.

Denote this design by \(\mathcal D_n\), and denote its corresponding minimax length and clipped frontier by \(\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star\) and \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star\), respectively.

We first compute the frozen optimized radius for this experiment.  Definition~\(\mathrm{def:concurrent\text{-}weights}\) gives \(u_2=1\).  The focal-arm part of the information envelope in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}design\text{-}scale}\) is independent of the schedule because the block-\(2\) propensity depends only on \(E\).  Consequently, for every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal B)\), nonnegativity of all other summands gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)
&\ge
8M^2\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac1{n^2}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
\left[\frac{1-p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}
{p_{2i}(z_1\mid H_{2i})}\right]\\
&=\frac{8M^2}{n}
\left\{
\varepsilon\frac{1-\delta_n}{\delta_n}
+(1-\varepsilon)
\right\}\\
&=8M^2\left\{1+\frac{1-2\varepsilon}{n}\right\}
\ge8M^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first inequality is uniform over \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\), so taking the schedule supremum in the definition of \(\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}\) is valid.  Since the drift-bias support function is nonnegative,
\[
\Psi_{\alpha,0}(v)
\ge \sqrt{\overline{\mathsf V}_{\mathcal D_n,0}(v)/\alpha}
\ge M\sqrt{8/\alpha}>2M
\]
for every feasible \(v\).  Clipping in Definition~\(\mathrm{def:average\text{-}frontier}\) therefore yields the exact equality
\[
\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M.
\]

We next construct an honest observed-data interval whose worst-schedule expected length tends to zero.  Conditional on \(E^c\), define the observable block-\(2\) score
\[
X_i=2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_1\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i}
-2\mathbf 1\{Z_{2i}=z_0\}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{2i},
\qquad
\widehat\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nX_i.
\]
Because both block-\(2\) propensities equal \(1/2\) on \(E^c\), sequential randomization gives, at every position,
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i\mid H_{2i},E^c]
=Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[X_i^2\mid H_{2i},E^c]
=2Y_{2i}(z_1)^2+2Y_{2i}(z_0)^2
\le4M^2.
\]
By Definition~\(\mathrm{def:target}\), the mean of the first display over \(i\) is exactly \(\tau_W\).  Hence
\(\Delta_i=X_i-\{Y_{2i}(z_1)-Y_{2i}(z_0)\}\) is a martingale difference conditional on \(E^c\).  For \(i<j\), iterated conditioning gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i\Delta_j\mid E^c]
=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
\left[\Delta_i
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_j\mid H_{2j},E^c]
\,\middle|\,E^c\right]=0.
\]
The second-moment bound and this orthogonality imply, uniformly over \(Y\in\mathcal Y_{M,0}\),
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}
[(\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W)^2\mid E^c]
=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_n,Y}[\Delta_i^2\mid E^c]
\le\frac{4M^2}{n}.
\]

Set
\[
\beta=\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}
=\frac{\alpha/2}{1-\alpha/2}>0,
\qquad
t_n=\frac{2M}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(t_n<2M\).  Define a deterministic observed-data kernel by reporting \(\{0\}\) on \(E\), and on \(E^c\) reporting
\[
J_n=
[\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-t_n,
  \Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)+t_n]
\cap[-2M,2M].
\]
The kernel is schedule independent.  Its reported set is always a nonempty closed interval because the projected center belongs to \([-2M,2M]\).  Bounded outcomes give \(\tau_W\in[-2M,2M]\), and projection onto this interval satisfies
\[
|\Pi_M(\widehat\theta_n)-\tau_W|
\le|\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W|.
\]
Moreover, the pointwise inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{|\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W|>t_n\}
\le\frac{(\widehat\theta_n-\tau_W)^2}{t_n^2}
\]
and the preceding second-moment calculation give
\[
P_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\notin J_n\mid E^c)
\le\beta.
\]
We make no coverage claim on \(E\).  Nevertheless, because \(P_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(E)=\varepsilon\) for every schedule,
\[
P_{\mathcal D_n,Y}(\tau_W\in I_K)
\ge(1-\varepsilon)(1-\beta)
=1-\alpha.
\]
Thus this kernel belongs to \(\mathcal C_\alpha\).  The singleton branch has zero length and \(\operatorname{len}(J_n)\le2t_n\), so uniformly over the schedule class,
\[
\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star
\le(1-\varepsilon)2t_n
=\frac{4M(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}.
\]
Combining this with \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) yields
\[
\frac{\mathfrak L_{\alpha,n}^\star}
{\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star}
\le\frac{2(1-\varepsilon)}{\sqrt{n\beta}}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
All primitive assumptions hold for every member of the sequence, while \(p_{\min,n}=\varepsilon/n\downarrow0\).  Therefore no positive lower-comparison constant depending only on \(\alpha\) can hold over the frozen design class.  In particular, the unresolved radius-to-modulus comparison cannot be true uniformly in the stated generality.
